message:
Address Palomar review: classification, provenance, Challenge docs

Classification
- Remove MSC2020 68V15. Using Lean to formalize this random-matrix
  inequality does not make theorem proving part of its mathematics; the
  remaining codes are 60B20, 60E15 and 47A30.

Provenance
- Record the MI-32 conjecture with a substantive relationship instead of
  background. The Open Problems in Numerical Linear Algebra entry, which
  states the problem in exactly the form formalized, is now `formalizes`,
  cited by commit permalink rather than the mutable main-branch URL, with
  Alex Townsend credited as the collection's compiler and editor. The
  originating paper, Latala-Swiatkowski, Norms of randomized circulant
  matrices, EJP 27 (2022) paper 80, whose Conjecture 4.3 is the selected
  result, is also `formalizes`, with a note that the paper proves only the
  Gaussian-mixture case, that Remark 4.5 is the structural model this proof
  deliberately diverges from, and that Theorem 4.1 is credited but not
  formalized. The derived result_origin stays source-based.
- Move GraphMatrices out of `sources` into `related_formalizations`. It is
  a prior Lean development reused as a dependency, not a mathematical
  source. It is identified immutably as
  DiarHaidary/Sharp-Bounds-for-Graph-Matrices@01994362f8543743d556e7544d2538e93c62c02b
  (public, MIT), with relationship builds-on and a note recording exactly
  what was reused (GraphMatrices.Walsh.polynomial_fourth_le_nine_pow, the
  scalar Boolean two-to-four inequality, plus the Walsh and finite-law
  vocabulary) and what was added here (MI32.hilbert_walsh_fourth_le, the
  dimension-free real Hilbert-space extension). No graph-matrix result is
  reused or re-claimed.
- vendor/graph-matrices/manifest.json previously recorded only a local
  Windows path; it now records the public repository and exact commit
  alongside the per-file SHA-256 hashes.

Challenge documentation
- Replace the stale claim that the Solution is incomplete. The theorem
  docstring now gives a plain-language account of the compared statement
  and says that the `sorry` is the intentional Challenge hole while the
  selected Solution declaration is completed and mechanically verified,
  depending only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

Also refreshes README, CONTINUE_HERE and docs/PROVENANCE, which still said
no submission had been made. No Lean statement, definition or proof changed;
the local gate is unchanged.
